input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects found by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each
flow is fully operable with keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable
controls, and consistent visible focus indicators. The audit report enumerates
the exact defects per flow; this epic clears that list. It delivers the
engineering half of the accessibility conformance strategy; the updated
conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) that reflects this
fixed state is tracked separately and must not be published before this work is
complete.

## Scope

- Remediate every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit for the four
  audited flows: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and
  pipeline run submission.
- Eliminate focus traps in the modals used by these flows (including focus
  loss on open/close) so keyboard users can enter, complete, and exit each
  modal.
- Make every control in the audited flows reachable and operable by keyboard.
- Apply consistent, visible focus indicators across the audited flows'
  controls, per HLR-2.
- Verify each flow end-to-end with keyboard-only walkthroughs (manual
  verification is part of this epic's engineering work).
- Keep existing Dashboard tests/CI passing; add regression coverage for the
  fixed keyboard behaviors where the repo's test conventions allow.

Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows can be completed end-to-end using keyboard
  alone, verified by a manual keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow.
- No focus traps remain in the modals of the audited flows; focus behavior on
  modal open and close is correct in each affected modal.
- Every control in the audited flows is reachable and operable by keyboard —
  the audit's "unreachable controls" findings are all remediated.
- Focus indicators are visible and consistent across all controls in the
  audited flows.
- Every defect in the audit report's per-flow enumeration is fixed, or has an
  explicitly recorded disposition (fixed / waived with rationale) — no
  silently dropped findings.
- Existing Dashboard CI and tests pass with the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — this epic's primary scope.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — bundled into this epic because the remediation is one sweep over the
  same four flows' shared UI surfaces and the same audit defect list; a
  separate epic would force a second pass over every flow.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed state of the four core Dashboard flows after the keyboard
accessibility remediation: the VPAT (conformance statement) and the product
documentation's accessibility statement. Two public-sector customers require
the updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the published
documents — not drafts — are the deliverable. The content must be technically
reviewed against the actual implemented fixes so the conformance claims are
accurate.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT to reflect the keyboard operability and focus-indicator state
  of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) after remediation, recording supported
  and any remaining unsupported criteria honestly.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the
  fixed state.
- Route both documents through technical review by the Dashboard engineering
  team against the shipped fixes, and through the standard documentation review
  and publication process.
- Republish the updated VPAT and accessibility statement to their
  customer-facing locations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT accurately reflects the post-remediation keyboard accessibility
  state of the four audited flows — every claim in it is backed by a shipped
  fix or a recorded, dispositioned limitation.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Both documents have been technically reviewed against the implemented
  fixes (review by the Dashboard engineering team recorded), per the
  docs-authoring review requirement.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished at their
  customer-facing locations (published, not draft).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review — this epic's entire scope.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

**Strategy**: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

## Triage Outcome

Not triaged as below-threshold or docs-only. The strategy spans two distinct
work streams across two components: code remediation in the Dashboard (HLR-1,
HLR-2) and substantive conformance-content authoring for Documentation (HLR-3 —
VPAT rewrite and accessibility statement republication, explicitly a customer-
facing deliverable in the problem statement). The multi-stream escape condition
for below-threshold applies, so the full decomposition path was run. It is not
docs-only because the Dashboard requires code changes.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Docs | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Dashboard keyboard accessibility remediation"] --> E002["E002 VPAT + accessibility statement republish"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by ALL Implementation epics) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must describe the fixed state, so the documentation epic is blocked by the Dashboard remediation epic. Per the docs-authoring priority exception, this edge does not push E002's P2 upstream — E001's P1 comes from HLR-1/HLR-2. |

No other edges:

- No Investigation epics — the strategy states there are no open questions and
  the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow (Step 3 decision rule:
  no unknown changes which epics exist or what they do).
- No onboarding chain — the Dashboard is an existing, Konflux-onboarded
  component per `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`,
  so no `repo-onboarding`, `license-validation`, or `konflux-onboarding` epics
  (Rules 19-22 do not fire). Rule 25 "build pipeline green" AC is not required
  because no `konflux-onboarding` epic is in any dependency chain.
- HLR-1 and HLR-2 are implemented as one epic (see traceability below), so
  there are no Implementation → Implementation edges.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission). |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 (bundled) | Bundled with HLR-1: the focus-indicator remediation is carried out in the same sweep over the same four flows' UI surfaces (same modals, same controls, same audit defect list). A separate epic would force a second pass over every flow and cannot ship independent user value — the audit treats visible focus as part of keyboard operability of these surfaces. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | docs-authoring epic; priority derived from strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2 per the docs-authoring priority exception. |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then) section, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria were derived
  from the HLRs and the problem statement; team ownership was taken from the
  architecture context (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard).
- **Documentation team assumption**: no owner is stated for the Documentation
  component. E002 is assigned to RHOAI Docs with a mandatory technical review by
  the Dashboard engineering team (Rule 24 AC); confirm the owning team before
  scheduling.
- **E001 size above the ~2-week guideline (kept whole deliberately)**: the four
  audited flows' defect remediation is estimated at ~2-3 weeks as a single
  sweep. Splitting per flow would duplicate work — the defects (focus traps in
  modals, unreachable controls, inconsistent focus indicators) cluster in
  shared Dashboard surfaces (modal/focus-management patterns common to all four
  flows), so one sweep avoids fixing the same shared component four times.
  **Conditional re-split trigger**: re-split by flow if the audit defect list
  resolves to materially more work than enumerated (e.g., remediation of the
  first flow uncovers >30 additional defects) or if the epic passes the
  2-week mark with two or more flows not yet started.
- **Customer schedule pressure (non-blocking)**: two public-sector customers
  require the republished VPAT before renewal. The renewal dates are outside
  this strategy's control; the decomposition puts the docs epic last (Rule 11)
  because the VPAT must reflect the fixed state. If the renewal date is close,
  consider shipping an interim conformance statement — a scope decision for the
  strategy owner, not a DAG change.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. Both epics are
internal to the platform; E002 is strictly sequenced behind E001.
